video_title: New Look Lakers, Luka’s Leadership & The Tatum-Brown Beef

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' offensive potential with Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: the ceiling to me is top five, if not top three in offensive rating
quotes.quote: I think this was the best opening impression you could ask for. Walker Kessler, 26 points, 12 for 12, first Lakers since Shaq to have 10 dunks in a game and it was so easy and effortless for that offense. I don't want to overreact to a game against the Warriors, they were undermanned, undersized, and they did make Walker Kessler look like Milt Chamberlain, as Shaq was saying after the game. But you play the schedule in front of you and a 20-point win in the NBA is a 20-point win. They took care of business, they were up 34 going into the fourth. So far, so good. Offensively, the ceiling to me is top five, if not top three in offensive rating and I think we saw that level of potential. They're just scratching the surface in my opinion, just because last year, Luka and Austin Reaves were both top 10 in points per possession as pick-and-roll ball-handlers. You just can't stop those two in the pick-and-roll.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler's defensive impact compared to Rudy Gobert
quotes.excerpt: the comparison for him since he entered the NBA has been Rudy Gobert
quotes.quote: The comparison for him since he entered the NBA has been Rudy Gobert. And that's a high expectation, particularly on the defensive end. Rudy Gobert is a defense onto himself. You throw him out there, you're basically going to have a top 10 defense annually, almost regardless of the type of pieces you're putting around him. I don't think Kessler is quite there defensively and even through these first few games, I'd put him at around like a B defensively and the Lakers are going to need him at an A or A-plus against the top offenses. But this is a guy if you look at since he entered the league, he's third in defensive field goal percentage allowed at the rim behind just Wembanyama and Chet. He does rate out statistically very similarly to Gobert through his first few years. Health has been a little bit of a concern, especially with last year, playing only 50 games. But I think realistic expectations, 14-15 points, 11-12 rebounds, he's consistently been in that two, two-and-a-half block range. And I think the goal for LA should be to be a top 10 defense with him out there. Now, when he's off the floor, I have major concerns. Kevon Looney, Mamu, it's going to be tough with the rim protection and the non-Kessler minutes, but if they're top 10 with him on the floor, plus the offense, that's where LA, I think can be a really good team.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's offensive strategy and playmaking evolution
quotes.excerpt: Luka loves setting the tone early, he is consistently the leading scorer in the league in first quarters
quotes.quote: The flow was good. With Luka, we know Luka loves setting the tone early, he is consistently the leading scorer in the league in first quarters and his strategy is, I'm going to score 12-15 points, whatever, in the first quarter and force the defense to adjust to me. And once they start putting two on the ball, once they start aggressively shading over, now I'm going to start picking you apart and that's when he gets the lobs, the skip passes to the corner. And so that's the way that Luka likes to approach offensively and I think we saw that with a big first quarter and then eventually, Golden State had to start shading over toward him and then that's when Kessler started getting even more lobs and some of the skip passes and stuff. So that to me was fine.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers offensive potential despite preseason struggles and turnover issues
quotes.excerpt: What we saw when there's actual stakes, like the offense is going to be fine.
quotes.quote: In the preseason, they were actually good defensively. Now granted, they played the Warriors twice, the Kings twice, but they were 10th in defensive rating and they were 23rd in offensive rating. So it was the offense that was in the mud, they were turning the ball over a ton and just didn't really get into a flow and a big part of that was who was available. Kessler only played a couple games, Luka and Austin were in and out. What we saw when there's actual stakes, like the offense is going to be fine.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Defensive personnel concerns and lineup limitations for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: You just can't go Luka, Mamu, Kessler as a front court.
quotes.quote: Defensively, I think with the combination of Jaden, Matisse, Quentin Grimes, a Duop Reath, once he returns, or maybe they put Jared Vanderbilt in the rotation, I do think they have solid perimeter defense, but you do just have to be really careful with the lineups that you put around Austin and Luka and this is where there is a segment of the fan base that was proposing starting Mamu and to me, I was like, you just can't go Luka, Mamu, Kessler as a front court. We haven't seen it and I think you could do it in bench configurations, but when they put Mamu out there, they're going zone. They're going 2-3 zone or 3-2 zone, they're trying to protect him in a zone and it's like, you can't do that consistently in starting minutes and closing minutes against the best offenses.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing the leadership maturation of Kobe Bryant and Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: Kobe the last half of his career was way different than Kobe the first half of his career.
quotes.quote: I think he's matured. I look at this is not the only example we have of this in NBA history where you go back to a guy like Kobe. Early in his career, the big thing with Kobe was he was this loner who wouldn't go out to the team dinners, he was constantly in his hotel room watching film or he'd be in the gym working out on the road, wasn't doing the team bonding stuff with the group and then at times was considered a bad teammate. And then later in his career, I think there was a real leadership shift with him where he finally realized like, sometimes including the guys or treating the guys a certain way, you'll get the best out of them. Kobe the last half of his career was way different than Kobe the first half of his career as a leader. I think with Luka, it's a similar thing where not the same dynamics, but it has been a maturation process.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic stepping up as a vocal leader for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: He's talked about recently having to be a more vocal leader and I think they've been putting out clips.
quotes.quote: Playing in LA, playing for the Lakers, I think we have seen this growth from him as a leader and he's talked about recently having to be a more vocal leader and I think they've been putting out a bunch of clips from practice and scrimmages and you see he's calling stuff out and I think being more vocal in a way that he wasn't necessarily before. But then you also look at the trip and how many guys organize that, pay for it out of their own pocket, have this extensive itinerary that is every meal, every thing that they're playing, they're racing bikes in the street, they're golfing, they're going on a rowing trip, like they're doing all these things together that Luka and his team organized. So, I thought like he's really stepped up in a major way and he's really grown into this.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic taking ownership of the team from LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: It is officially his team and it's understandable too because anytime LeBron's in the room, LeBron is LeBron.
quotes.quote: It is officially his team and it's understandable too because anytime LeBron's in the room, LeBron is LeBron. Like LeBron is going to have a certain cachet. It technically was LeBron's team when Luka got there and so I'm sure on some level there was always that just like, yeah, it's LeBron's job, let him do it.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's leadership and team-building initiatives
quotes.excerpt: I think it's good for competitiveness, like I was talking about this with Sean, it's like, you know, check gets
quotes.quote: I enjoy a young guy being unafraid and uncowed in that moment and, you know, I think it's good for competitiveness, like I was talking about this with Sean, it's like, you know, check gets thrown to the ground by De'Aaron Fox and he just sits there and is just like, I'm stoic, I'm not going to react, whereas like to me, I'm like, you should react. You should get pissed. You should put hands on that little dude. Like, I, you know, and and so I like both like Luka's not going to back down. I like the young guy getting into it and I even love the stuff after the game. It's just like, yo, I'm going to see this dude again. We play these guys three, four times a year. So, there is no where to hide after saying what I said. So you got to go out and do it on the court and, you know, I think that's only good for people like us who love watching the ultimate competitors go at it.

quotes.speaker: Big Wos
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Tatum's handling of the Jaylen Brown trade situation
quotes.excerpt: To pretend you didn't know this dude would not be on the team next year is complete bullshit.
quotes.quote: I just got finished watching the Elizabeth Holmes doc from Nathan Fielder. Excellent work, and I encourage everybody to see this, but this reminds me of an Elizabeth Holmes situation where you can say something that can mean two things. Jason Tatum can say he didn't know where Jaylen Brown would end up and when it would be executed. But to pretend you didn't know this dude would not be on the team next year is complete and utter bullshit. Because Jason Tatum did not call Brad Stevens and say, get this motherfucker off my team. He did not do that. He is not really that type of dude. He wouldn't do that. However, if Jason Tatum really wanted Jaylen Brown back, the organization would have known and they would never have traded Jaylen Brown.
